The slice is `rows[start:end + 1]` instead of `rows[start:end]`, so every page returns page_size+1 rows and the last row of page N reappears as the first row of page N+1 — sequential pages overlap by one row at each boundary.

Ignores the MINOR_UNITS table and hardcodes quantize exponent Decimal('0.01'); for order_totals('1234','0.08','JPY') it returns VAT ¥98.72 and gross ¥1332.72 instead of the integer-yen ¥99 and ¥1333, so JPY invoices carry an illegal fractional yen and are off by ~0.28 yen.

Input redact('mail first.last@acme.com now') returns 'mail first.[EMAIL] now', leaking 'first.': the email local-part class [A-Za-z0-9]+ excludes '.', so the match starts at 'last@acme.com' and the 'first.' fragment survives.
Input md_to_html('1 < 2 & 3') returns '1 &lt; 2 & 3' instead of '1 < 2 & 3': _escape replaces '<' -> '<' before escaping '&', so the '&' in '<' is then turned into '&', double-escaping the '<'.

Input highlight('f("a", "b")') returns 'f(<str>"a", "b"</str>)' instead of two spans: the string pattern uses a greedy `".*"`, so it spans from the first quote to the LAST quote, swallowing '", "' between the two literals.

Results are yielded in os.walk's arbitrary readdir/filesystem order with no sorting; the spec required a deterministic sorted sequence, so two runners over identical trees can emit files in different orders and produce different cache keys.

The cascade loop runs `range(backup_count, 0, -1)`, so it renames path.{backup_count} to path.{backup_count+1} instead of deleting it; with backup_count=3 you end up retaining path.1..path.4 (four backups) instead of exactly three.

Acquisition is a check-then-create TOCTOU race: between the `os.path.exists` test and the later `open(path, 'w')`, a second process can create and write the lockfile, and then both processes proceed as lock holders — the create step must be a single atomic os.open(..., O_CREAT | O_EXCL) instead.
